brief.analysis: The trade bets silver falls back toward gold, but the strongest case against it is that both metals have structurally re-rated: silver roughly tripled in 2025 on solar and electrification demand while gold hit records on relentless central-bank buying and a move away from the dollar. The old five-year average of the silver-to-gold price relationship was set before either of those shifts, so it is very likely no longer the right target — and the ratio has already reached its 200-day average, meaning the extra push the model wants is fighting a live, two-sided change in the world.
brief.report_line: We are short silver-versus-gold expecting a snap-back to the old five-year norm, but flag high regime risk: silver's demand-driven re-rating and record central-bank gold buying may have permanently moved that norm, so the position is sized down or passed rather than pressed.

brief.analysis: The trade bets metals-and-mining stocks give back their lead over the broad S&P 500 and revert to the old five-year relationship, but the strongest counter is that these miners are directly levered to the same gold, silver and copper complex now in a record structural bull, so the reversion could stall well short of the old average. The mean has probably drifted higher rather than moved wildly, and the 200-day target is already met with only two clean historical episodes behind the base rate — tradeable, but on a half-size footing given real commodity-cycle risk.
brief.report_line: We are short metals-and-miners versus the S&P 500 for a partial mean-reversion, sized down: the group has already reverted to its 200-day average and the underlying metals bull could keep miners richer than their old five-year norm, so we take the easy part of the move and avoid pressing toward the flat mean.
